en.title: Past time expressions
en.goal: Learn time markers for talking about the past, as preparation for the passé composé.

lessons.ontem-anteontem-semana-passada: Yesterday, the day before yesterday and last week
lessons.fim-de-semana-mes-ano-passados: Last weekend, last month and last year
lessons.dois-dias-atras-ja-recentemente: Two days ago, this morning, already and recently

phrases.scenario: Someone asks what you did yesterday, and you visited a museum. What do you answer?

phrases.t: Last week, I ate at a restaurant.
phrases.scenario: Someone asks what you did that was special last week — you ate at a restaurant. What do you say?
Someone asks what the weather was like last weekend — it rained a lot. What do you answer?
You want to know whether a friend has ever been to Paris. What do you ask?

phrases.t: The day before yesterday, I visited Paris.
Last month, I traveled to France.
This morning, I had a coffee.

dialogue.title: What did you do yesterday?
lines: I worked in the morning, and in the afternoon I played sports.
We went to the movies with friends.

hier-vs-semaine-derniere.title: "Hier" or "la semaine dernière"?
hier-vs-semaine-derniere.body: Hier points to a specific day (yesterday). La semaine/le week-end dernier(-ère) points to a wider period (last week or last weekend). They all go well with the passé composé you've already seen: hier, j'ai visité un musée / la semaine dernière, j'ai mangé au restaurant.

quest-ce-que-tu-as-fait-wh-in-situ.title: "Qu'est-ce que tu as fait hier ?" also becomes "T'as fait quoi hier ?"
quest-ce-que-tu-as-fait-wh-in-situ.body: In very everyday speech, this question often comes out like this: t'as fait quoi hier ? — "qu'est-ce que" disappears, "quoi" moves to the end, and "tu as" contracts to "t'as". Three simplifications at once, all very common together. In the exercises here, keep using the full form — it's the one the exercises ask for.
examples: what did you do yesterday? (very everyday speech)

review.why: 'déjà' = 'already' in statements, 'ever' in questions ('Tu as déjà visité Paris ?'); PT gloss is only 'já'.
Present perfect with 'ever' is the natural English equivalent of 'Tu as déjà...'; 'Have you already visited Paris?' is also possible.

review.pt: Semana passada eu comi num restaurante.
review.en: Last week, I ate at a restaurant.
The day before yesterday, I visited Paris.
review.why: 'avant-hier' has no short EN equivalent; 'the day before yesterday' is the standard.

review.pt: Hoje de manhã, eu tomei um café.
review.en: This morning, I had a coffee.
review.why: 'j'ai bu' = drank; 'had a coffee' is more natural.

review.pt: Eu trabalhei de manhã, e à tarde eu fiz esporte.
review.en: I worked in the morning, and in the afternoon I played sports.
review.why: 'faire du sport' = 'play sports / exercise'; 'exercised' also fine.

review.pt: A gente foi ao cinema com amigos.
review.en: We went to the movies with friends.

review.pt: o que você fez ontem? (fala bem cotidiana)
review.en: what did you do yesterday? (very everyday speech)
